cohort: 206 pregnancies from 134 self-identified individuals aged 18-50 diagnosed with vulvodynia with symptom onset prior to pregnancy
finding: This online survey of individuals with vulvodynia found that reported symptom severity generally remained unchanged or decreased during pregnancy, but increased postpartum, and that use of topical corticosteroids decreased during pregnancy compared with before and after pregnancy.
mod_finding: Of the pregnancies in the study, 67% resulted in vaginal birth and 33% resulted in cesarean birth.
